approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds a fresh surplus of molecular graphs from its highest-scoring accepted survivors, using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. A fingerprint Gaussian process learns from all accepted observations, and correlated posterior draws select each evaluation batch. Accepted offspring compete for later breeding. Before pool admission, the Parent confirms that each canonical molecular identity is stable, normalizing verified aliases and rejecting unresolved representations. Its bond-change operator alters one existing bond order; it has no direct move that changes a ketone position while retaining the surrounding carbon skeleton.
approach.novelty: Add a ketone-position move that transfers a terminal carbonyl oxygen to an adjacent methylene carbon. Both the old and new carbonyl must have carbon neighbors, so the move retains the molecular formula, carbon skeleton and ketone class while changing the oxygen position. It becomes an alternative within the existing bond-change operator. Earlier siblings protected carbonyl atoms, exchanged aromatic nitrogen positions or moved branches around aromatic rings. This experiment instead offers a coordinated positional change within a saturated carbon framework.

hypothesis: Offer direct transfer of a ketone carbonyl oxygen to an adjacent methylene as an alternative within change_bond, preserving molecular formula, the carbon skeleton and ketone class while exposing a new carbonyl position to the inherited fresh-pool selector.

finding_summary.headline: Ketone shifts reached evaluation: four direct tests gave one gain, two ties and one loss
finding_summary.insights:
A ketone can move within these observed ring and acyclic carbon frameworks without destroying its class or changing the molecule's composition. That establishes a usable positional neighborhood, while the direct score results show that utility depends on the particular position and molecular family. Exposure is narrow: only 140 of 7,723 bond-change calls had an eligible source, and only four of 4,290 scored proposals isolate the transfer itself. The available evidence therefore supports access to this neighborhood more strongly than a reliable optimization benefit.

The largest whole-search improvement, a 0.083867 gain in one sitagliptin run, occurred with no selected ketone transfer at all. Two eligible calls instead chose the original bond-order mode, changing subsequent random consumption. This rules out interpreting that gain as an observed benefit of the shifted oxygen; selected molecules and later search history changed together. The four direct comparisons are the evidence for local positional utility. Their unchanged composition also explains why they do not establish repair of the chemical liabilities identified by the molecular assessment. Broader useful exposure, consistent improvement and completion of the full score panel remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The oxygen-position mechanism happened. All 70 executed shifts retained the molecular formula, carbon skeleton and ketone class and produced a different, stable molecular identity. Forty-eight pool entries retained the exact immediate shifted graph, covering 39 distinct identities. Four reached evaluation as sole changes to accepted scored molecules: a DRD2 transfer improved its source by 0.003265, a median_2 transfer lost 0.003475, and two ring transfers tied. A fifth evaluated history included an additional atom replacement and lost 0.002890 against its generating parent. All five entered the survivor population; none improved the incumbent.

Every generated pool and batch was full, but deco_hop in seed 2 timed out after 240 of 300 evaluations, leaving 14 of 15 task sessions complete. The two complete seed macros average 0.553584 versus their matched parent's 0.553199, a paired gain of only 0.000385, with one seed lower and one higher. This is below the registered 0.002 target on the available complete seeds; the full three-seed effect cannot be evaluated. The parent completed the entire panel. The changed whole-search chemistry still contains reactive bonds, large repeated assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry.

molecular.headline: Aromatic polycycles and crowded amines retain reactive bonds, oversized repeats and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The observed output contains substantial aromatic and heterocyclic chemistry: compact bridged aryl carbonyls, linked carbonyl heteroaromatics, halogenated polyamines, larger aza rings, and fluorinated aryl dicarbonyl heterocycles. Ring-closure text rates span 0.9782–0.9966 and aromatic-presence rates span 0.9471–0.9897; these are proportions of proposal strings containing the corresponding feature, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Functional-group diversity and differing core families justify moderate overall structural diversity, but the highest-scoring excerpts repeatedly modify related cores. Familiar medicinal-chemistry fragments coexist with N–halogen, O–halogen and peroxide bonds, crowded aminals, unusual bridges, and very large repeated assemblies, making overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak. No proposal string specifies an atom stereocentre or formal charge. Neutral strings do not imply absence of potentially basic amines. All five objectives have supplied trajectories; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The observed deco_hop seed-2 trajectory stops at evaluation 240, so its chemistry and comparisons with a parent trajectory reaching 300 describe partial coverage. Other supplied child task/seed trajectories reach 300. All child and parent trajectory files were read. Structural counts were derived passively with RDKit from those recorded molecules and are reproducible in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0010-15-improve-L01-molecular.audit.json. No new molecule, score, objective requirement or mechanism-activation judgment is introduced. Score gradients below are associations within the observed search histories, not isolated causal effects or claims of experimental activity.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact aromatic carbonyl assemblies with densely bridged nitrogen-containing cores, small alkyl/alkoxy groups and fluorinated aromatic appendages. Proposal median size is 25 heavy atoms, the same as the parent; mean SMILES length is 45.0, ring-closure presence 0.9805 and aromatic presence 0.9793. The leading molecule has 25 heavy atoms, a bridged aza core and an N-fluoro carboxanilide. Other high excerpts retain an aroyl ketone or thioester; later products include fused N–N and N–O rings. The conventional methoxy-substituted indole carboxanilide in the initial set gives way to more demanding bridged structures. The parent leading family was also a compact bridged aryl/heteroaryl ketone, with recorded best 0.4463521672202675; the child leading N-fluoro amide reaches 0.4478476056206344. This is a change within a similar chemical region, with additional N–halogen occurrences: 243 of 870 proposals versus 187 of 870 in the parent.
liabilities: The leading amide has an N–F bond rather than an ordinary N–H or N–alkyl substituent. High numerical score does not establish its stability or suitability as a medicinal compound.

Thioesters, late N–N/N–O rings and short bridged connections need specific synthesis and stability assessment. The generated series does not specify configurations where potential atom stereocentres arise.
missing_features: The smallest low-scoring fragments omit the connected aromatic, nitrogen-containing core and carbonyl-bearing appendage shared by the stronger examples.

The stronger excerpts provide limited ordinary alternative core geometries that preserve this compact functional arrangement. Broader comparable amide/ketone structures without unusual N–F or bridged heteroatom connections remain underrepresented; an exact unseen preferred topology cannot be inferred.

The compact bridged N-fluoro amide CCc1cc2c3c(C)c1CN2C(C(=O)N(F)c1ccc(F)cc1)=CN3 scores 0.4478476056206344, the aroyl ketone CCc1cc2c3c(C)c1OCN2C(C(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1)=CN3 0.4349635367667153, and the thioester CCc1cc2c3c(C)c1OCN2C(C(=O)Sc1ccc(F)cc1)=CN3 0.4238198477630873. The final N–N-ring/N-fluoro-amide product COc1cc2c(c(OC)c1CF)C=C(C(=O)N(F)c1ccc(F)cc1)NN2 scores 0.3630045684864706, whereas C=C and ClBr score 0.0. This supports a coherent compact arrangement, without establishing that N–F, additional bridging or one carbonyl position independently improves the objective.

per_task.generated_character: The best excerpts join carbonyl-bearing O/N heteroaromatics through an NH linkage, with short annulated carbon bridges, aryl halogens, an aryl cyanate group and peroxide–halogen appendages. The best molecule has 32 heavy atoms, but the entire observed proposal stream has median 52 and maximum 119 heavy atoms. liabilities: O–O–Cl, O–O–F and O–halogen appendages are chemically reactive motifs. The aryl cyanate and short annulations add unresolved synthetic and stability questions.

Repeated polyaromatic/dicarbonyl assemblies carry a large synthetic burden and unmeasured solubility or conformational liabilities. Their continuing evaluation at substantial scores does not establish useful medicinal properties.

High-scoring output gives few clearly tractable alternate implementations of that arrangement without unusual short annulations, cyanate or peroxide–halogen chemistry. The observed fluoromethyl variant shows that the O–O–halogen chain is already replaceable with little score change; broad stable alternatives are still limited.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

finding_summary.headline: Ketone shifts reached evaluation: four direct tests gave one gain, two ties and one loss
finding_summary.insights:
A ketone can move within these observed ring and acyclic carbon frameworks without destroying its class or changing the molecule's composition. That establishes a usable positional neighborhood, while the direct score results show that utility depends on the particular position and molecular family. Exposure is narrow: only 140 of 7,723 bond-change calls had an eligible source, and only four of 4,290 scored proposals isolate the transfer itself. The available evidence therefore supports access to this neighborhood more strongly than a reliable optimization benefit.

The largest whole-search improvement, a 0.083867 gain in one sitagliptin run, occurred with no selected ketone transfer at all. Two eligible calls instead chose the original bond-order mode, changing subsequent random consumption. This rules out interpreting that gain as an observed benefit of the shifted oxygen; selected molecules and later search history changed together. The four direct comparisons are the evidence for local positional utility. Their unchanged composition also explains why they do not establish repair of the chemical liabilities identified by the molecular assessment. Broader useful exposure, consistent improvement and completion of the full score panel remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The oxygen-position mechanism happened. All 70 executed shifts retained the molecular formula, carbon skeleton and ketone class and produced a different, stable molecular identity. Forty-eight pool entries retained the exact immediate shifted graph, covering 39 distinct identities. Four reached evaluation as sole changes to accepted scored molecules: a DRD2 transfer improved its source by 0.003265, a median_2 transfer lost 0.003475, and two ring transfers tied. A fifth evaluated history included an additional atom replacement and lost 0.002890 against its generating parent. All five entered the survivor population; none improved the incumbent.

Every generated pool and batch was full, but deco_hop in seed 2 timed out after 240 of 300 evaluations, leaving 14 of 15 task sessions complete. The two complete seed macros average 0.553584 versus their matched parent's 0.553199, a paired gain of only 0.000385, with one seed lower and one higher. This is below the registered 0.002 target on the available complete seeds; the full three-seed effect cannot be evaluated. The parent completed the entire panel. The changed whole-search chemistry still contains reactive bonds, large repeated assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry.

finding_summary.headline: Ketone shifts reached evaluation: four direct tests gave one gain, two ties and one loss
finding_summary.insights:
A ketone can move within these observed ring and acyclic carbon frameworks without destroying its class or changing the molecule's composition. That establishes a usable positional neighborhood, while the direct score results show that utility depends on the particular position and molecular family. Exposure is narrow: only 140 of 7,723 bond-change calls had an eligible source, and only four of 4,290 scored proposals isolate the transfer itself. The available evidence therefore supports access to this neighborhood more strongly than a reliable optimization benefit.

The largest whole-search improvement, a 0.083867 gain in one sitagliptin run, occurred with no selected ketone transfer at all. Two eligible calls instead chose the original bond-order mode, changing subsequent random consumption. This rules out interpreting that gain as an observed benefit of the shifted oxygen; selected molecules and later search history changed together. The four direct comparisons are the evidence for local positional utility. Their unchanged composition also explains why they do not establish repair of the chemical liabilities identified by the molecular assessment. Broader useful exposure, consistent improvement and completion of the full score panel remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The oxygen-position mechanism happened. All 70 executed shifts retained the molecular formula, carbon skeleton and ketone class and produced a different, stable molecular identity. Forty-eight pool entries retained the exact immediate shifted graph, covering 39 distinct identities. Four reached evaluation as sole changes to accepted scored molecules: a DRD2 transfer improved its source by 0.003265, a median_2 transfer lost 0.003475, and two ring transfers tied. A fifth evaluated history included an additional atom replacement and lost 0.002890 against its generating parent. All five entered the survivor population; none improved the incumbent.

Every generated pool and batch was full, but deco_hop in seed 2 timed out after 240 of 300 evaluations, leaving 14 of 15 task sessions complete. The two complete seed macros average 0.553584 versus their matched parent's 0.553199, a paired gain of only 0.000385, with one seed lower and one higher. This is below the registered 0.002 target on the available complete seeds; the full three-seed effect cannot be evaluated. The parent completed the entire panel. The changed whole-search chemistry still contains reactive bonds, large repeated assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry.

Pool molecule occurrences bearing N-halogen/O-halogen/O-O bonds are 6,881/6,034/2,383 of 68,640; corresponding emitted counts are 489/385/141 of 4,290. No pool or emitted molecule specifies atom stereochemistry. Mean size changes from the primary parent are +0.134878 heavy atoms in pools and +1.458042 in emissions, with median zero and ranges -113 to +76 / -102 to +68; these reflect mixed production operators, while the immediate shift's size change is exactly zero. The supplied molecular assessment still finds reactive bonds, demanding polycycles/repeated assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry; the conserved ketone move does not establish their repair.

observable_measurements.value: All 70 independently reconstructed immediate shift products satisfy serialize/parse/serialize stability and agree with the inherited checked_molecule and unchanged pool_identity_admission helper. All 68,640 admitted pool identities and 4,290 emitted identities are parseable fixed points; every novelty decision, generating-parent score, emission key and available feedback key reconciles without discrepancy. The guard records 74,540 unchanged stable admissions and two confirmed stable alias normalizations, with zero unstable-identity or graph-mismatch rejections; 414 attempts fail the preceding graph check. The two normalized aliases are in the unchanged seed-1 deco_hop history and are unselected. All 150 initial occurrences are stable. Thirteen source-distinct shifts are rejected by the ordinary duplicate scopes: seven emitted/initial and six temporary-pool duplicates. Four of the global duplicate rejections reverse earlier recorded transfer pairs. An additional reversed pair is pooled because its final identity is still globally novel; temporary proposals are not globally marked seen. There are no symmetry-equivalent shifts credited as activation, no inconsistent normalized collision and no admitted instability. All 4,280 received offspring feedback records join correctly. Ten additional emissions in the timed-out final deco_hop batch have trajectory scores but no candidate feedback; the log retains exactly those ten pending keys, so acceptance into candidate memory is not claimed. Paired no-option replay on all 7,583 recorded immediate inputs, using identical specified audit RNG states for Child and Parent, produces identical graph snapshots and final RNG states. This checks matched-input behavior rather than recovering an unlogged historical RNG state. Six complete task/seed histories with no eligible call also match the Parent molecule-for-molecule and score-for-score across all 300 evaluations each. Source comparison confirms the identity helpers and all non-active methods remain unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Ketone shifts reached evaluation: four direct tests gave one gain, two ties and one loss
finding_summary.insights:
A ketone can move within these observed ring and acyclic carbon frameworks without destroying its class or changing the molecule's composition. That establishes a usable positional neighborhood, while the direct score results show that utility depends on the particular position and molecular family. Exposure is narrow: only 140 of 7,723 bond-change calls had an eligible source, and only four of 4,290 scored proposals isolate the transfer itself. The available evidence therefore supports access to this neighborhood more strongly than a reliable optimization benefit.

The largest whole-search improvement, a 0.083867 gain in one sitagliptin run, occurred with no selected ketone transfer at all. Two eligible calls instead chose the original bond-order mode, changing subsequent random consumption. This rules out interpreting that gain as an observed benefit of the shifted oxygen; selected molecules and later search history changed together. The four direct comparisons are the evidence for local positional utility. Their unchanged composition also explains why they do not establish repair of the chemical liabilities identified by the molecular assessment. Broader useful exposure, consistent improvement and completion of the full score panel remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The oxygen-position mechanism happened. All 70 executed shifts retained the molecular formula, carbon skeleton and ketone class and produced a different, stable molecular identity. Forty-eight pool entries retained the exact immediate shifted graph, covering 39 distinct identities. Four reached evaluation as sole changes to accepted scored molecules: a DRD2 transfer improved its source by 0.003265, a median_2 transfer lost 0.003475, and two ring transfers tied. A fifth evaluated history included an additional atom replacement and lost 0.002890 against its generating parent. All five entered the survivor population; none improved the incumbent.

Every generated pool and batch was full, but deco_hop in seed 2 timed out after 240 of 300 evaluations, leaving 14 of 15 task sessions complete. The two complete seed macros average 0.553584 versus their matched parent's 0.553199, a paired gain of only 0.000385, with one seed lower and one higher. This is below the registered 0.002 target on the available complete seeds; the full three-seed effect cannot be evaluated. The parent completed the entire panel. The changed whole-search chemistry still contains reactive bonds, large repeated assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry.

molecular_assessment.headline: Aromatic polycycles and crowded amines retain reactive bonds, oversized repeats and unspecified stereochemistry.

Ring-closure text rates span 0.9782–0.9966 and aromatic-presence rates span 0.9471–0.9897; these are proportions of proposal strings containing the corresponding feature, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Functional-group diversity and differing core families justify moderate overall structural diversity, but the highest-scoring excerpts repeatedly modify related cores. Familiar medicinal-chemistry fragments coexist with N–halogen, O–halogen and peroxide bonds, crowded aminals, unusual bridges, and very large repeated assemblies, making overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak. No proposal string specifies an atom stereocentre or formal charge. Neutral strings do not imply absence of potentially basic amines. All five objectives have supplied trajectories; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The observed deco_hop seed-2 trajectory stops at evaluation 240, so its chemistry and comparisons with a parent trajectory reaching 300 describe partial coverage. Other supplied child task/seed trajectories reach 300. All child and parent trajectory files were read. applicability_conditions: The mechanism requires the explicitly registered ketone adjacent to an ordinary implicit-H methylene whose other heavy neighbor is carbon. It excludes aromatic carbonyl endpoints, aldehydes, amides, esters, acyl halides, isotopic/radical/charged endpoints, explicit-H targets and tagged donor/target centers. Other parts of the same molecule may still contain those unrelated groups.

Both ring and acyclic ketone contexts may qualify. Keeping the carbon skeleton and ketone class does not certify ring strain, conformation, synthesis, stability of the entire molecule or a favorable carbonyl placement. Existing amine, aromatic and other bond arrangements remain present but their relationship to the moved oxygen deliberately changes.

Observed availability is concentrated in a subset of accepted molecular families. The fixed inherited parent allocator and selector can starve this channel, and opportunity counts must not be reported as actual evaluated exposure. No task identity, preferred molecule size, scored library or new oracle stream is used.

The existing carbonyl-protection cluster concerns exclusion of endpoint replacements, while the two positional-edit clusters concern aromatic nitrogen exchange and single-bond branch movement on aromatic carbons. The proposed two-edge ketone-oxygen transfer between nonaromatic carbons is a distinct production mechanism; those sibling interventions are not inherited by this Child.

The equal conditional choice within change_bond is part of the new local proposal channel. It changes search RNG consumption only when a qualifying source exists; other operator probabilities and the entire accepted-memory/posterior/acquisition stack remain frozen. Whole-run gains cannot be assigned to an unobserved alternative from the original stochastic path.

The read-only constructions use only recorded Parent graphs and the installed RDKit convention. Their formula and identity checks establish local feasibility on those inputs, not measured scores, global novelty, complete formal activation or transfer to arbitrary graph/parser families.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds a fresh surplus of molecular graphs from its highest-scoring accepted survivors, using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. A fingerprint Gaussian process learns from all accepted observations, and correlated posterior draws select each evaluation batch. Accepted offspring compete for later breeding. Before pool admission, the Parent confirms that each canonical molecular identity is stable, normalizing verified aliases and rejecting unresolved representations. Its bond-change operator alters one existing bond order; it has no direct move that changes a ketone position while retaining the surrounding carbon skeleton.
approach.novelty: Add a ketone-position move that transfers a terminal carbonyl oxygen to an adjacent methylene carbon. Both the old and new carbonyl must have carbon neighbors, so the move retains the molecular formula, carbon skeleton and ketone class while changing the oxygen position. It becomes an alternative within the existing bond-change operator. Earlier siblings protected carbonyl atoms, exchanged aromatic nitrogen positions or moved branches around aromatic rings. This experiment instead offers a coordinated positional change within a saturated carbon framework.

research_intent.falsifier: The construction claim is refuted if a selected ketone shift uses a site outside the registered rule, changes any atom identity or unrelated edge/property, changes formula or carbon skeleton, changes ketone count/class, or credits an identity-equivalent representation as a changed positional isomer. Failed or symmetric attempts that follow the ordinary rejection path are not construction violations, but do not count as activated positional alternatives. A complete run with eligible opportunities but no changed pool product fails pool activation; changed pool products with no emission retaining the immediate shifted graph leave evaluated activation unestablished. An admitted identity instability, inconsistent novelty/pending key, changed no-option RNG behavior, altered top-level operator law, or non-active Layer modification is an implementation mismatch. Correctly executed and evaluated shifts can still tie or lose to their sources; that is negative utility evidence rather than failed construction. A paired macro gain below the supplied 0.002 target refutes the registered score-benefit expectation without erasing independently confirmed graph activation. Inadequate pool completion or additional cost is reported even if some positional edits succeed.
research_intent.implementation_change: Edit only the bound candidate optimize.py in graph_pool. Add a pure helper enumerating eligible tuples (carbonyl_bond_index, carbonyl_carbon_index, oxygen_index, target_carbon_index), sorted lexicographically in the current source atom/bond indexing. A donor is a nonaromatic C=O double bond between neutral, nonisotopic, radical-free atoms. Its carbon is untagged for chirality, permits implicit hydrogens, has heavy degree three and total hydrogen count zero, and its two neighbors other than the terminal oxygen are both carbon attached by single bonds. The oxygen has heavy degree one and total hydrogen count zero. A target is one of those adjacent carbons, must be neutral, nonisotopic, radical-free, nonaromatic and untagged for chirality, must permit implicit hydrogens with no explicit H count, and must have heavy degree two, exactly two total hydrogens, only single incident bonds and only carbon heavy neighbors. Thus the donor and product are both ketones; amide/ester/acyl-halide carbonyls and targets that would create those classes are outside the new move. Enumerate these tuples at the start of GraphOperators.change_bond without editing the source or consuming RNG. If no tuple exists, run the inherited change_bond body with exactly its original choices, order and RNG consumption. If tuples exist, make one uniform choice from the ordered modes [bond_order, ketone_shift]. In bond_order mode, execute the original bond selection and bond-order alternative rule unchanged after this mode draw. In ketone_shift mode, choose one tuple uniformly from the sorted list, copy the source with RWMol, remove the donor-carbon/oxygen double bond and add a target-carbon/oxygen double bond. Preserve all atom objects, atomic numbers, charges, isotopes, explicit-H settings, chiral tags and every other bond. Ordinary sanitization then changes the donor's implicit H count from zero to two and the target's from two to zero. Return this one edited graph through the inherited mutate validation and bounded retry; do not add a second edit, force a different site after failure, prelabel a product, or special-case a task. Keep the top-level mutation names and weights, crossover and walk laws, CONFIG values and mutate return interface unchanged; the realized operator remains change_bond with a passive bond_change_mode identifying the new branch. Reset the receipt list once per outer breeding attempt and attach it to the existing provenance so invalid, duplicate, pooled, emitted and accepted outcomes can be joined. Record detailed source/product invariants for attempted ketone shifts; all-call opportunity counts and the original operator trace must remain available to distinguish a failed inner attempt from a realized shift. Diagnostics may serialize copies but must not change live graphs, RNG or any selection decision. Keep checked_molecule, pool_identity_admission, read_molecule, every other graph operator, accepted archive/survival/parent allocation, posterior representation and inference, within-pool acquisition, emission/feedback semantics, pool target, atom bounds, retries and valid fallbacks at the bound Parent implementation. research_intent.mechanism: Offer direct transfer of a ketone carbonyl oxygen to an adjacent methylene as an alternative within change_bond, preserving molecular formula, the carbon skeleton and ketone class while exposing a new carbonyl position to the inherited fresh-pool selector.

Its identity-admission mechanism leaves every evaluated molecule and score unchanged from its own Parent. The molecular assessment identifies limited alternatives around recurring aromatic/carbonyl arrangements, while the actual change_bond implementation only changes one existing bond order. It cannot perform the registered two-bond oxygen reattachment in one local operation. A read-only audit of the Parent's fifteen saved task logs finds the exact eligible ketone/methylene rule in 137 of 4350 emitted graphs, with 145 site options, and in the primary parent of 2097 of 75607 outer breeding attempts. Those repeated draws involve 60 distinct accepted primary-parent identities with 62 distinct source/site options. Unscored construction on the 145 emitted-source options and 62 distinct breeding-parent options yields source-distinct, parse/serialize-stable products with unchanged formula and atom/bond counts in every case. This is a feasibility and opportunity audit, not a new trajectory, global-novelty result or oracle comparison. The carbonyl-protection sibling n-9bee44b1c9c3 preserved C=O endpoints yet changed adjacent functional relationships and lost 0.034753 in paired macro mean. The nitrogen-position sibling n-9edaa26007c3 supplies one directly observed incumbent gain from a positional edit, whereas the aromatic-branch sibling n-2bb53b5f7b44 shows that intact positional alternatives can activate without meeting their score target. These observations motivate access to a specific new ketone neighborhood, without assuming that carbonyl retention or positional changes are intrinsically beneficial.
